title: Roadmap set to boost trade with Malaysia
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan and Malaysia on Friday agreed on a roadmap to deepen trade and investment relations, identifying key areas of cooperation at a business conference.

Malaysian High Commissioner Dato Mohammad Azhar Mazlan, who led the ‘Malaysia-Pakistan Business Engagement 2026’, said bilateral trade could be increased substantially from $1.5 billion to $5bn through enhanced commercial engagement and greater private sector participation.

He stressed the need to translate the longstanding friendship into stronger trade and investment partnerships, noting Pakistan’s importance as a major South Asian trading partner.

He identified artificial intelligence, education, manufacturing and services as promising areas for collaboration, noting that Pakistan’s geographical position as a gateway to Central Asian markets and its young population were major strengths.

Referring to opportunities in the edible oil and halal products sectors, he encouraged Pakistani businesses to explore Malaysia, citing Pakistani investment in halal gelatine production there as an example of successful cross-border ventures. He said a win-win approach should remain central to economic engagement.

Minister for Investment Qaiser Ahmed Sheikh said Pakistan and Malaysia shared considerable potential to expand commercial engagement, develop joint ventures and strengthen their presence in regional and global markets.

He identified information technology, artificial intelligence, advanced technology, manufacturing, value-added industries, mining and minerals, agriculture, food processing and halal products as sectors offering substantial potential for joint ventures.

He said Malaysia’s technological expertise could complement Pakistan’s natural resources, workforce and large consumer market. Pakistan, he added, welcomed high-quality Malaysian investment that contributes to industrial development, technology transfer, employment generation and export growth.

title: Short-term inflation surges 11.38pc
text:
ISLAMABAD: Short-term inflation rose by 11.38 per cent year-on-year in the week ending Oct 15, driven largely by higher food prices, according to official data released by the Pakistan Bureau of Statistics on Friday.

Of the 51 essential items monitored during the week, prices of 23 commodities increased, while seven declined, the data showed. Meanwhile, the prices of 21 items remained unchanged from the previous week.

Short-term inflation has remained in double digits for several consecutive weeks, largely due to persistent increases in petroleum prices.

The Sensitive Price Index (SPI), which tracks short-term inflation, slightly fell 0.04pc week-on-week, reflecting price fluctuations in both food and non-food items.

Unwilling to ease the petroleum levy, the government has continued to raise petrol and diesel prices daily. The surge in energy costs is not only fuelling inflationary pressures but also indirectly boosting sales tax collections through higher prices of goods and services.

This is cost-push inflation, in which rising energy costs are followed by increases in food prices. As a result, households are under pressure from higher consumer prices.

The items whose prices increased the most over the previous week included pulse gram (4.97pc), wheat flour (3.36pc), chicken (3.31pc), eggs (0.99pc), pulse mash (0.98pc), pulse masoor (0.95pc), firewood (0.69pc), shirting (0.58pc), cooked daal (0.55pc), diesel (0.47pc), LPG (0.42pc) and tea prepared (0.28pc).

The items whose prices declined week-on-week included tomatoes (23.05pc), onions (4.90pc), bananas (2.59pc), petrol (0.70pc), rice basmati broken (0.65pc), sugar (0.62pc) and gur (0.36pc).

On an annual basis, the items that recorded the highest price increases included onions (75.19pc), LPG (68.95pc), electricity for Q1 (58.59pc), petrol (49.60pc), diesel (43.98pc), wheat flour (35.13pc), chicken (20.77pc), chilies powder (15.55pc), mutton (14.90pc), beef (12.27pc), bread plain (9.02pc) and tea prepared (8.36pc).

In contrast, tomatoe prices fell by 63.65pc, followed by potatoes (39.93pc), sugar (23.20pc), eggs (19.83pc), salt powder (14.86pc), pulse masoor (8.97pc), gur (8.92pc) and pulse moong (7.83pc).

title: 20 local IT firms attend TechCrunch
text:
WASHINGTON: Pakis­tan showcased about 20 technology companies at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026 in San Francisco, seeking to expand its tech industry’s international reach, attract investment, and strengthen commercial ties with the US.

Pakistan’s Ambassador to the US, Rizwan Saeed Sheikh, urged participating companies to leverage their presence in Silicon Valley to build lasting commercial partnerships and explore investment opportunities in the US market.

He also assured them of the full support of Pakistan’s diplomatic missions in the United States for building business connections with American partners, according to a press release from the Embassy of Pakistan in Washington.

The ambassador highlighted the growing capabilities of Pakistan’s technology industry and emphasised the importance of strengthening Pakistan-US cooperation in information technology, innovation and digital entrepreneurship.

He encouraged companies to position Pakistan as a competitive, reliable partner in the global digital economy. The Pakistan Pavilion at the three-day event, held from Oct 13 to 15 at Moscone West in San Francisco, featured around 20 tech showcasing their products, innovative solutions across various technology sectors.

During his interaction with company representatives on Thursday, Rizwan Sheikh was briefed on their products and efforts to expand their presence in the US market.

TechCrunch Disrupt is a major technology and start-up conference that brings together early-stage founders, entrepreneurs, software professionals, venture capitalists and industry leaders.

title: ‘Pakistan among 10 states bearing brunt of hunger crisis’
text:
ISLAMABAD: Pakistan is among the 10 countries bearing the brunt of the global hunger crisis, with climate-related disasters, economic hardship, displacement and shrinking humanitarian funding pushing vulnerable communities deeper into food insecurity, according to a new report released by international humanitarian organisation Action Against Hunger.

The report, Ten Largest Global Food Crises, released on Friday in connection with World Food Day, warns that an estimated 10.6 million people in Pakistan will require humanitarian assistance in 2026, despite ongoing recovery efforts and improvements in some macroeconomic indicators.

Globally, approximately 177 million people live in the 10 countries where hunger is most concentrated, while acute hunger has doubled over the past decade, affecting 266 million people across 47 countries, says the report.

The countries facing the largest food crises are Nigeria, Congo, Sudan, Yemen, Afghan­istan, Myanmar, Bangladesh, Pakistan, South Sudan and Syria.

Report sees 10.6m Pakistanis needing humanitarian assistance in 2026

In Pakistan, persistent poverty, high food inflation, rising living costs, limited employment opportunities and declining household incomes continue to erode families’ purchasing power. Unfavourable agricultural prices and broader economic instability have further undermined livelihoods, leaving millions struggling to afford adequate food.

As humanitarian needs outstrip available resources, vulnerable households are increasingly resorting to damaging coping strategies, including cutting food consumption, selling productive assets and withdrawing children from school to cope with financial pressures.

The report cautions that these measures may provide temporary relief but can deepen poverty, undermine children’s education and nutrition, and weaken families’ ability to recover from future shocks.

Limited access to healthcare, nutrition services, clean water, sanitation and hygiene (WASH), and social protection is compounding the crisis, particularly in rural and disaster-affected areas. Persistent poverty and acute malnutrition remain major drivers of humanitarian needs, while cuts to support services and livelihood programmes are further eroding community resilience.

Pakistan’s exposure to climate-related disasters remains a major source of food insecurity. Recurrent floods, droughts, heatwaves, glacial lake outburst floods (GLOFs) and increasingly erratic monsoon rainfall have damaged infrastructure, reduced agricultural production and weakened livestock-dependent livelihoods.

Crop losses and prolonged dry spells have also increased households’ reliance on markets for food at a time when many families have limited purchasing power. Several districts are experiencing prolonged drought conditions, adding to concerns about agricultural output and rural incomes.

The report warns that seasonal hardships can intensify these pressures. The lean season from December 2025 to March 2026, characterised in some areas by extended winter conditions and heavy snowfall, was identified as a period likely to worsen food insecurity by restricting access to markets and essential resources.

Insecurity and regional tensions are adding another layer of pressure to Pakistan’s already fragile food security situation.

According to the report, localised insecurity in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa and Balochistan continues to disrupt livelihoods, restrict access to markets and hamper humanitarian operations.

title: Peshawar mourns after roof collapse snuffs out 31 lives
text:
• Teacher, 30 students among the dead; around 30 injured treated at Lady Reading Hospital • Chief secy forms fact-finding committee to probe incident, suggest preventive measures • Governor tells PM school owner in custody; safety audit of schools across province ordered • President, PM call for best treatment for the injured; Unicef pledges psycho-social support

PESHAWAR: At least 30 children and a schoolteacher lost their lives and dozens of others were injured after the roof of a multi-storey private school collapsed in the Dir Colony area on Thursday, plunging the city into mourning.

The incident occurred at the Al-Khair Education Centre, loc­a­ted off Outer Circular Road. Res­cue officials said the ceiling of a classroom came down on students after the roof of a higher floor collapsed, crumpling the two storeys.

Bilal Ahmad Faizi, a spokesman for Rescue 1122, said when the emergency response teams arrived at the scene, they found that one roof had collapsed onto another, trapping several children inside.

Lady Reading Hospital spokesperson Muhammad Asim confirmed that 30 students and a female teacher had lost their lives. According to the official list of casualties, a total of 61 people were brought to the facility, 30 of whom were discharged after treatment.

Speaking to Dawn, Samiullah, a parent who rushed to the site after hearing about the incident, said he had rescued three girls, all under the age of eight.

“I received a call from home at around 8:50am and reached the site about 10 minutes later, at aro­und 9am. We have six children studying at the school,” he said.

“When I saw the building, I tho­ught my son, who was in a ground-floor classroom beneath the collapsed first floor, had also died. However, he had left the classroom to drink water,” he added.

Resident Sohail told AFP that “everyone began screaming in panic” after his niece managed to find her way home after escaping the building to inform them of the collapse. “When I arrived at the scene, I saw around 10 to 15 children trapped beneath the rubble, with debris piled up to their necks. We quickly pulled them out,” he said.

The provincial chief secretary has constituted a fact-finding committee to probe the incident and tasked it with submitting a report within seven days.

The committee includes the secretary of the transport department, Zubair Ahmed, and chief engineer of the communication and works department, Jamshid Ali Khan.

KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi also sought a detailed rep­ort and directed the authorities to determine the cause of the collapse. “The loss of precious lives of innocent children is an extremely painful tragedy,” the statement said.

He also announced a compensation of Rs1 million for those who lost their lives and a compensation of Rs200,000 for those who sustained injuries in the incident. The governor prayed for the speedy recovery of the injured children and directed the authorities concerned to provide them with the best possible medical facilities.

In another statement on his X account, Mr Kundi added that he had also directed a structural safety audit of educational institutions across the province to identify potential risks and ensure that immediate corrective measures are taken wherever necessary. “We cannot allow the safety of our children to be compromised,” Mr Kundi wrote.

Meanwhile, funeral prayers for the children and their teacher were offered in Peshawar, and were attended by the governor, besides hundreds of others, including relatives of the deceased students.

Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif also expressed deep grief over the loss of lives and sought a report on the tragic incident. The PM telephoned the KP gove­­rnor to discuss the inc­ident, the PM’s Office said.

Briefing the PM, the governor said the school’s owner had been arrested, and an investigation had been initiated. The PM directed that all aspects of the incident be thoroughly examined and that act­ion be ensured against those resp­onsible in accordance with the law.

PM Shehbaz also extended condolences and sympathies to the bereaved families of those who lost their lives in the incident and directed that the best possible medical facilities be provided to the injured and that all possible assistance and support be extended to the affected families.

In a similar statement, Pres­ident Asif Ali Zardari expressed sorrow over the tragic incident, and extended his heartfelt condolences to the bereaved families.

He directed the authorities to ensure the provision of the best possible medical facilities to the injured and extend all possible assistance to the affected families.

In a statement, Unicef Pakistan representative Pernille Ironside said their thoughts were with the injured children. “We wish them a swift and full recovery. Unicef stands ready to support the government’s response by providing psycho-social support to affected children, families and communities,” she said.

Unicef also called for urgent act­ion to ensure that all schools meet building safety standards. These standards must be strictly enforced to prevent such tragedies in the future, the representative said.

Amin Ahmed in Islamabad also contributed to this report

title: Power users face Rs33bn FCA hit in Nov bills
text:
ISLAMABAD: The power division on Thurs­day projected an additional fuel cost adjustment (FCA) of Rs2.56 per unit for electricity consumed in September, translating into an estimated Rs32.7 billion burden on consumers in November bills.

In a statement, the division said the adjustment would have been significantly higher, by around Rs3.44 per unit, but targe­ted load management hel­ped contain the price shock.

“The Ministry of Energy (Power Division) has aver­ted a potential Rs5-6 per unit hike in the September 2026 Fuel Price Adjust­ment (FPA) through timely measures, including targeted load management, limiting the projected adjustment to Rs2.56 per unit despite rising international fuel prices and constraints on LNG supplies,” the statement said.

Over the past two mon­ths, the power division has started issuing advance estimates before the Cen­tral Power Purchasing Agency (CPPA) formally makes the regulatory filing required for monthly fuel cost adjustments.

“Targeted load management and other measures helped limit the impact of expensive fuels used for power generation, saving consumers from an additional burden of up to Rs3.44 per unit,” the division said.

It confirmed that targeted load management of around two to two-and-a-half hours during September helped reduce reliance on costly alternative fuels, including furnace oil and high-speed diesel and contain the anticipated increase in the FCA.

The division added that supplying imported re-gasified liquefied natural gas (RLNG) for power generation at domestic gas prices had further eased the burden on consumers by 83 paise per unit.

“Consequently, the September FPA is expected to be Rs1.45 per unit higher than that of August,” the statement said. The August FCA was Rs1.11 per unit, while the estimated financial impact of the September adjustment is Rs32.7bn on consumers’ electricity bills in November.

The power division said international fuel prices had risen sharply amid regional conflicts and disruptions to fuel supply chains following the closure of the Strait of Hormuz. Brent crude prices had surged beyond $120 per barrel, compared with the benchmark of around $70 per barrel assumed while determining the base electricity tariff.

Despite Qatar’s declaration of force majeure, Pakistan continued efforts to meet its RLNG requirements through available contracted supplies and additional spot cargoes where necessary, it added.

The division also claimed that the combined impact of fuel price adjustments and quarterly tariff adjustments during January-August had been limited to 65 paise per unit, equivalent to an increase of only 1.9pc over the base electricity tariff.

It attributed this partly to tariff rationalisation measures and an additional electricity consumption package for industrial and agricultural consumers, which it said encouraged greater use of power from the national grid.

However, industrial consumers have disputed the claimed benefits of the support package. They contend that the Rs22.96 per unit marginal cost rate benefits only a limited number of consumers, while an actual marginal cost of around Rs34 per unit results in an additional burden of about Rs11 per unit being fed into the average tariff, putting a burden on all consumers.

At their request, Nepra last week held a public hearing on revising or suspending the incremental package, but a decision is still awaited.

The power division said it was continuing to monitor developments in international fuel markets and supply chains while taking measures to minimise the impact of external price shocks on electricity consumers.

title: TTAP ‘suspends all talks’ until meeting with Imran
text:
• Gives Achakzai sole authority over future negotiations with govt• PTI leaders privately criticise handling of talks• Calls emerge from within party for changes in interim leadership

ISLAMABAD: The Tehreek-i-Tahafuz-Ayin-i-Pakistan (TTAP) on Thursday announced the suspension of all negotiations with the government, stressing that there would be “no talks” until a meeting with PTI founder Imran Khan was arranged and information about his health was provided.

The opposition alliance said all authority for future negotiations would rest solely with its chairman, Mehmood Khan Achakzai.

The decision was taken at a leadership meeting held at Mr Achakzai’s residence, where participants reviewed the political situation arising from the imposition of emergency and governor’s rule in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa.

Political tensions between the federal government and the opposition, particularly PTI, had remained high in recent weeks after the party announced a long march demanding the release of its incarcerated founder. The march, initially billed as one towards Islamabad, remained confined to KP before fizzling out following the imposition of governor’s rule.

The TTAP strongly condemned the measures in KP, describing them as a “robbery” and a midnight assault on the Constitution and the people’s mandate.

It demanded their immediate withdrawal, saying the decision was an insult not only to the people of KP but to those of all provinces. The alliance also anno­unced that it would challenge the move in the Peshawar High Court.

The TTAP condemned terrorism in all its forms and expressed support for the National Action Plan. It demanded that, instead of adopting new policies, the joint resolution of the Aman Jirga approved by the KP Assembly be implemented.

The alliance also sought the immediate release of non-functional Chief Minister Sohail Afridi, Assembly Speaker Babar Saleem Swati, PTI provincial president Junaid Akbar and detained members of the National and provincial assemblies and other party leaders.

PTI had reported their detention on Oct 11, shortly after the Centre imposed emergency and governor’s rule in the province.

The alliance also demanded the release of Imran Khan’s sisters, who have been detained for nearly three weeks under the Maintenance of Public Order (MPO) Ordinance, as well as access to the former prime minister by his family and doctors.

The TTAP also blamed the deteriorating law and order situation in Balochistan on an “unrepresentative” provincial government and “failed” federal policies. It urged the authorities to resolve the province’s problems through dialogue rather than force.

The alliance also said it would approach international human rights organisations and the United Nations over alleged restrictions on judicial independence, curbs on the media and violations of human rights and the Constitution.

The federal government imposed emergency under Article 232 and governor’s rule under Article 234 on Oct 11 after the cabinet discussed the security situation in KP and accused the provincial government of “deliberate disengagement from the fight against terrorism”.

Meanwhile, some PTI leaders privately criticised the handling of negotiations with the government and the party’s response to the imposition of governor’s rule.

Speaking to a group of journalists, the leaders blamed Mr Achakzai’s “egoistic approach” for contributing to the failure of talks, arguing that he was among the few opposition figures capable of concluding an agreement but had declined to participate directly in key meetings.

They claimed that MWM chief Allama Raja Nasir Abbas had taken the initiative in bringing the government and opposition to the negotiating table after little progress had been made by PTI’s own leadership.

According to one of the leaders, the plan following the announcement of the long march had been for then-chief minister Sohail Afridi to build political pressure through mobilisation while the party leadership pursued negotiations with the Centre.

However, he claimed little effort was made to initiate negotiations until Mr Abbas intervened and that the march was subsequently delayed by a week to allow talks to proceed.

The PTI figures also questioned the party’s preparedness for governor’s rule, pointing out that it took several days to approach the courts against the measure.

One leader said the party should have prepared its legal challenge in advance and provided clear instructions to its provincial lawmakers immediately after the Centre’s decision.

They also said discussions had begun within PTI about changes to the party’s interim leadership and some members argued that experienced political negotiators should be given a greater role.

“Imran Khan had suggested that Barrister Ali Zafar become PTI chairman, but he refused, saying that he wanted to focus on the cases of PTI. Moreover, there are politicians like Malik Aamir Dogar, who knows how to negotiate, but he is even not allowed to chair the meetings of parliamentary party,” a party leader said.

However, the leaders acknowledged that JUI-F chief Maulana Fazlur Rehman had clearly communicated his position during the political negotiations, including his refusal to participate in the long march.

title: ECP rejects Punjab’s plea to delay LG polls
text:
• After four-year delay, commission resolves to issue election schedule ‘immediately’ • Province had proposed polls in three phases from April next year

ISLAMABAD / LAHORE: Putting its foot down after four years of delay, the Election Commission of Pakistan (ECP) on Thursday rejected Punjab’s plea to postpone local government ele­ctions until April next year and deci­ded to issue the schedule immediately.

Earlier this month, the electoral body proposed holding local government elections in Punjab on Dec 14 and sent a draft schedule to the Punjab chief secretary for consultation.

However, the Punjab government on Wednesday proposed holding the elections in three phases on April 4, 11 and 18, citing smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions expected during December and January.

On Thursday, the ECP rejected the provincial government’s request. The decision was taken at a meeting chaired by Chief Election Commissioner Sikandar Sultan Raja.

Commission members Nisar Ahmed Durrani, Babar Hassan Bharwana and retired Justice Ikramullah Khan, as well as ECP Secretary Omar Hamid Khan and other senior officers, attended the meeting.

The commission was briefed that the Punjab government had responded on Oct 14 to the ECP’s Oct 2 letter and draft election programme.

Citing dense fog and severe cold in December, followed by the start of Ramazan in February, the provincial government proposed holding local government elections in three phases in April 2027.

The ECP termed the provincial government’s response unsatisfactory, saying consultations had been completed on Aug 20, when the provincial authorities had agreed to hold local government elections in Punjab between Dec 15 and Jan 15, 2027.

“Now, the provincial government wants to change the proposed timeframe,” the commission said.

The statement added that keeping its constitutional and legal responsibilities in view, the ECP had decided to hold local government elections in Punjab and issue the schedule immediately.

It directed its office to promptly submit the draft election programme for approval.

The ECP also said it had asked the provincial government to provide lists of officers to be appointed as district returning officers, returning officers and assistant returning officers. Expressing disappointment over the failure to provide the lists so far, the commission directed the provincial government to submit them within a week.

The Punjab Local Government and Community Development Department wrote to the ECP on Wednesday, seeking a delay in the local government polls.

The letter, conveying a ministerial committee’s decision, cited expected smog, dense fog and adverse winter weather conditions during December and January, followed by the start of Ramazan in February, as reasons for not holding the elections as scheduled.

The letter said the cabinet’s ministerial committee had held its second meeting on Oct 5, during which it discussed the ECP’s draft election schedule at length. The committee considered scenarios arising from likely harsh weather conditions and Ramazan, it added.

The ministerial committee proposed holding the local government elections in phases to facilitate the deployment of election staff and security personnel, the transportation of polling materials, administrative oversight and access for voters.

The phased approach would also help avoid adverse weather conditions typically experienced during December and January, as well as the period immediately following Ramazan, the letter said.

It added that the Punjab cabinet had considered the committee’s recommendations early on Wednesday and approved a proposal to hold the elections in three phases on April 4, 11 and 18, 2027, all Sundays.

The cabinet also decided that the allocation of districts among the three phases could be discussed and mutually agreed upon with the ECP at a dedicated meeting, taking into account administrative, logistical, security and geographical considerations, as well as weather conditions, the letter said.

title: Three die as Istanbul sees heaviest rain  in 80 years
text:
ISTANBUL: Istanbul was battling on Thursday to recover from flooding caused by what officials described as the heaviest rainfall in at least 80 years, as the toll rose to three dead and five missing.

The rain began lashing Turkiye’s largest city in earnest on Wednesday morning and intensified throughout the day, causing chaos and flash flooding, with footage showing cars being dragged away by the fast-flowing waters. “We are talking here about the highest level of precipitation in Istanbul since records began in 1942,” Istanbul governor Davut Gul said.

The death toll from the floods rose to three when authorities found a man’s body near a park in the Kagithane area on the European side, Gul’s office said in a statement. The storm also claimed the life of a 14-year-old boy who was electrocuted when he stepped into a puddle in the Balat area. He was rushed to hospital but medical personnel were unable to save him, officials said. Five others were missing, officials said.

Schools closed through weekend as authorities urge residents to stay indoors

In Beykoz, on Istanbul’s Asian side, DHA news agency said another man had died after falling into a well while trying to drain the water at a school construction site. There was no immediate official confirmation of his death.

Istanbul municipal teams and firefighters were carrying out cleanup operations at schools, football pitches, garages and other sites on Thursday, pumping water out of flooded areas and clearing mud, a photographer reported.

On Wednesday evening, the governor said schools would be shut across Istanbul until Monday, urging people to stay home “unless absolutely necessary” and advising those living in basement properties “to spend the night on safer, higher floors”. Dramatic footage posted online on Wednesday and collated by DHA showed a line of parked cars in the northern Sariyer district being pushed into the torrent of muddy water, where they were swept away.

Another showed people being hauled from the raging waters to safety through a first-floor window, while elsewhere two people with umbrellas were seen stepping into the shovel of a large mechanical digger, which took them away.

Power and water cuts have also hit areas of the city, notably in Sariyer where shopkeepers could be seen trying to salvage their goods from the mud, a journalist said.

Heavy rainfall in the nearby province of Sakarya caused a two-storey villa on the banks of a stream to collapse in Sapanca neighbourhood. As the house had been evacuated earlier, no one was killed or injured.

And in the neighbouring Kocaeli province, a stream overflowed in Gebze district, sweeping away a driver who was later rescued by emergency workers with ropes.
